speaker: Doctor
text: THANK YOU for sharing that information. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me if the skin lesions are itchy, painful, or just visible?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That camping trip is concerning; did you have any contact with a tick or a small animal while in Minnesota? Also, can you describe exactly what the skin lesions look like, such as their shape and color?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis.

Based on the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions, recent camping in Minnesota, and the migratory joint pain followed by acute monoarticular wrist involvement, this is consistent with disseminated Lyme disease. I am ready to proceed with treatment recommendations.
